{{Short description|French chemist (born 1961)}}

[[File:Philippe Sautet.jpg|thumb|Philippe Sautet, Member of the French Academy of sciences]]
'''Philippe Sautet''' (born 8 May 1961 in [[Salon-de-Provence]], [[France]]) is a French [[chemist]]. He was elected to the [[French Academy of Sciences|French Academy of sciences]] on 30 November 2010.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.academie-sciences.fr/academie/membre/Sautet_Philippe.htm |title=Philippe Sautet - les Membres de l'Académie des sciences |access-date=2019-08-08 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110909221436/http://www.academie-sciences.fr/academie/membre/Sautet_Philippe.htm |archive-date=2011-09-09 |url-status=dead }}</ref> He was a research director at the CNRS and works in the chemistry laboratory of the [[École normale supérieure de Lyon]] where he devoted a large part of his scientific activity to [[molecular modelling]].<ref>La Rechercher n°458 (décembre 2011) Spécial chimie n°73. p.39.</ref> He is currently a professor at the [[University of California, Los Angeles]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Sautet Group - UCLA|url=http://www.seas.ucla.edu/~sautet/|last=Group|first=Sautet|website=www.seas.ucla.edu|access-date=2017-08-03|publication-date=}}</ref>

== Biography ==
Philippe Sautet is an engineer from the [[École Polytechnique|École polytechnique]] (Paris). He prepared his thesis at the University of Paris (Orsay) from 1985 to 1988 under the supervision of [[Odile Eisenstein]].<ref>Sautet P. (1988). Etude théorique de la transmission électronique au long d’une chaîne polymère. Thèse de l'Université Paris XI.</ref> He was then a researcher at the [[Centre national de la recherche scientifique|CNRS]] in the Institut de Recherche sur la Catalyse ([[Villeurbanne]], France) from 1988 to 1995, then Visiting Scientist at [[Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory|Lawrence Berkeley Laboratory]] ([[Berkeley, California|Berkeley]], California) from 1991 to 1992. Upon his return from the United States, he was a lecturer and then professor at the École Polytechnique from 1993 to 2005. He then took over the management of UMR 5182 (Chemistry Laboratory of the École normale supérieure de Lyon, France) between 2003 and 2010. This is a research team of 80 people.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.ens-lyon.fr/CHIMIE/|title=Accueil — Laboratoire de Chimie de l'ENS de Lyon}}</ref> He is also Director of the Institut de Chimie de Lyon, FR CNRS 3023 (1,000 people) since 2007.

== Scientific works ==
Philippe Sautet<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://perso.ens-lyon.fr/philippe.sautet/Philippe_Sautet.html|title=Philippe Sautet|access-date=2019-08-08|archive-date=2019-08-22|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190822182124/http://perso.ens-lyon.fr/philippe.sautet/Philippe_Sautet.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> specialises on the theory of [[heterogeneous catalysis]]. The study of surfaces also contributes to the current development of nanotechnologies. He was interested in electronic structures at the solid gas interface, modeling of the elementary stages of heterogeneous catalysis and tunnel microscopy.
[[File:Benzène image STM.jpg|thumb|An image of benzene by tunneling microscopy: on the left, the experimental image; on the right, the calculated image]]
An image of [[benzene]] by tunneling microscopy: on the left, the experimental image; on the right, the calculated image.

He was responsible for the first simulation of a tunneling microscope image for an adsorbed molecule and the first demonstration of the capabilities of the simulation method developed.<ref>P. Sautet and C. Joachim "Calculation of the benzene on Rhodium STM images by the ESQC technique". Chemical Physics Letters, 185, 23 (1991).</ref>

In 1998, he published one of the first reactivity studies in heterogeneous catalysis by periodic DFT calculation. This work helps to understand the difference in reactivity between [[palladium]] and [[rhodium]].<ref>D. Loffreda, D. Simon, P. Sautet "Molecular and dissociative chemisorption of NO on palladium and rhodium (100) and (111) surfaces: a density-functional periodic study". J. Chem. Phys., 108, 6447-6457 (1998).</ref>

He is then the author of the determination of the nature of the [[active site]] for [[silver]] [[Epoxide|epoxidation]]. He then demonstrated the presence of a thin layer of [[oxide]] under reaction conditions.<ref>C.I. Carlisle, D.A. King, M.-L. Bocquet, J. Cerda, P. Sautet. “ Imaging the surface and the interface atoms of an oxide film on Ag(111) by scanning tunneling microscopy : experiment and theory ”. Physical Review Letters, 84, 3899 – 3902 (2000)</ref>

He is studying for the first time the adsorption of a [[Chirality|chiral]] molecule on a metal surface, thus showing the establishment of an asymmetric 2D network and its implications for [[enantioselective]] heterogeneous catalysis.<ref>L. A. M. M. Barbosa and P. Sautet. Stability of Chiral Domains produced by adsorption of Tartaric acid isomers on the Cu(110) surface : a periodic density functional study. J. Am. Chem. Soc. 123, 6639-6648 (2001).</ref>

He published the first paper on gamma [[Aluminium oxide|alumina]] surface modeling under realistic hydration conditions and determined the nature of the surface as a function of the pre-treatment temperature.<ref>M. Digne, P. Sautet, P. Raybaud, P. Euzen and H. Toulhoat. "Hydroxyl groups on g-Alumina Surface : a DFT Study”. J. Catal. 211, 1-5 (2002).</ref>

He then comes to model small aggregates of [[gold]] deposited on oxides. He can then study the nucleation sites.<ref>A. del Vitto, G. Pacchioni, F. Delbecq and P. Sautet. “Au atoms and dimers on the MgO(100) surface: a DFT study of nucleation at defects”. J. Phys. Chem. B 109, 8040-8048 (2005).</ref>

He then succeeds in making a complete mechanistic study of the [[regioselectivity]] of a hydrogenation reaction on a polyfunctional molecule. This makes it possible to understand the key role of the [[desorption]] step of the partially [[Hydrogenation|hydrogenated]] product on selectivity.<ref>D. Loffreda, F. Delbecq, F. Vigné and P. Sautet “Chemo-Regioselectivity in Heterogeneous Catalysis : Competitive routes for C=O and C=C hydrogenations from a theoretical approach” J. Am. Chem. Soc. 128, 1316-1323 (2006).</ref>

At the same time, he performed the first modeling of [[Organometallics|organometallic]] complexes grafted on an alumina surface and included the grafting mechanism. It also performs a coupled experimentation-theoretical determination of the structure of the reactive site at the surface.<ref>J. Joubert, F. Delbecq, P. Sautet, E. Le roux, M. Taoufik, C. Thieuleux, F. Blanc, C. Coperet, C. Thivole-Cazat, Basset J.M. "Molecular understanding of alumina supported single-site catalysts by a combination of experiment and theory". J. Am. Chem. Soc. 128, 9157 (2006).</ref>

[[Palladium]] carbide formed under the reaction conditions of [[acetylene]] hydrogenation.
[[File:Carbure palladium.jpg|thumb|Palladium carbide formed under the reaction conditions of acetylene hydrogenation]]
It then shows that during the selective hydrogenation of acetylene, the surface of the palladium catalyst is not metallic, but that a surface carbide is formed, responsible for the high selectivity in partial hydrogenation. This demonstration uses in situ spectroscopy combined with simulation.<ref>Detre Teschner, Zsolt Révay, János Borsodi, Michael Hävecker, Axel Knop-Gericke, Robert Schlögl, D. Milroy, S. David Jackson, Daniel Torres, Philippe Sautet. "Understanding Pd Hydrogenation Catalysts: When Nature of the Reactive Molecule Controls the Nature of the Catalyst Active Phase Angewandte Chemie" 47, 9274 (2008)</ref>

It then demonstrates the ability to predict the selectivity of a heterogeneous catalytic reaction by a correlation approach on a polyfunctional molecule ([[Saturated and unsaturated compounds|unsaturated]] [[aldehyde]]).<ref>David Loffreda, Françoise Delbecq, Fabienne Vigné and Philippe Sautet. "Fast Prediction of Selectivity in Heterogeneous Catalysis from extended Brönsted-Evans-Polanyi Relations: A Theoretical Insight". Angewandte Chemie International Edition, 48, 8978 (2009).</ref> This work was highlighted by a News and Views in the journal Nature.

It recently shows that, when hydrogenating a double bond on [[platinum]], the coordination of this [[double bond]] on the surface is not necessary. It highlights a new six-centre mechanism for heterogeneous catalytic hydrogenation of [[butadiene]], where the double bond approaches above the [[hydride]]. The discussion of the various possible situations shows that this new mechanism is favoured over the one with prior coordination.<ref>F. Delbecq, D. Loffreda, P. Sautet. "Heterogeneous Catalytic Hydrogenation: Is Double Bond/Surface Coordination Necessary?" J. Phys. Chem. Lett., 1, 323-326 (2010).</ref>

== Distinctions ==
He was awarded the Raymond Berr Prize from the École Polytechnique in 1985. He was awarded the [[CNRS Bronze Medal|CNRS bronze medal]] in 1991 and the [[CNRS Silver Medal|CNRS silver medal]] in 2007. He was awarded the Catalysis Division of the [[Société chimique de France|Chemical Society of France]] in 1993 and the [[Descartes-Huygens Prize]] from the [[Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences]] in 1998. He received the Paul Pascal Prize from the French Academy of sciences in 2008.

He was elected to the French Academy of sciences in 2010.

The [[Société chimique de France|Société Chimique de France]] awarded him the Grand Prix Pierre Süe 2012 for his work in theoretical chemistry and catalysis, as well as for his actions in the service of chemistry in Lyon.

== Scientific publishing ==
Philippe Sautet is or has been editor of many international scientific journals:

*    Publisher of the journal "catalysts and catalysed reactions" 2002-2004.
*    Member of the international editorial board of "[[Surface Review and Letters]]" since 2000
*    Member of the international editorial board of the "[[New Journal of Chemistry]]" 2002-2005
*    Member of the international editorial board of the "[[Journal of Molecular Catalysis]]" 2002-2005
*    Member of the international editorial board of "[[Surface Science]]" since 2006
*    Member of the international advisory board of "[[ChemCatChem]]" since 2009
*    Member of the international advisory board of "[[Topics in Catalysis]]" since 2010
*    Member of the international advisory board of "[[Catalysis Letters]]" since 2010
